clue.text: After blackout attempt to return to work piled up

indicators.note: the 'out' glued to 'black' in 'blackout' says those five letters are knocked out of order
to return is to go back, so the word for an attempt is written backwards

parts.note: an attempt is a go, as in 'have a go'

explanation.surface: After a power cut, someone tries to get back to work and finds it has piled up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'blackout' as two words: 'out' is the anagram signal on 'black', and 'to return' sends the attempt backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlog is an accumulation of unfinished tasks waiting to be dealt with.

clue.text: Airline blunder about runway's terminal is infantile

parts.note: BA is British Airways

indicators.note: the word for blunder goes about the single letter

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake

indicators.note: the terminal letter of a word is its last one

explanation.surface: An airline's mistake on the runway at the terminal is childish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' looks like the airport building but only picks the last letter of 'runway's'. BISH is old British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Babyish and infantile both mean childish, behaving like a small child.

clue.text: Instrument discovered in dilapidated English castle

indicators.note: a dilapidated building is in ruins, so its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An old instrument is found inside a ruined English castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A celesta is a keyboard instrument whose hammers strike metal plates.

clue.text: Smooth parts of purple velvet

indicators.note: the letters come from parts of the two words, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Smoothing out some sections of purple velvet cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To level something is to make it flat and even, as a verb of making smooth.

clue.text: Italian patriot ultimately fell in a big raid that went wrong

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the jumbled raid letters
a raid that went wrong is in disorder, so these letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the word fell

explanation.surface: An Italian patriot finally fell during a large raid that failed.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi was the soldier hero of Italian unification in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Nut, before time, put a touch of lemon in 5 down US way

indicators.note: the built word comes before the letter for time
the letter is put in the middle of the American spelling

parts.note: 5 down is FIBRE, which Americans spell with -ER at the end

indicators.note: just a touch of the word lemon means only its first letter

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a nut, then a dash of lemon, done the American way.
explanation.walkthrough: '5 down' points to the answer FIBRE; 'US way' asks for its American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A filbert is a hazelnut, especially the cultivated kind.

clue.text: Expression of disapproval about British strength of character

indicators.note: the exclamation goes about the abbreviation

parts.note: 'fie!' is an old exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Tutting at the British people's moral backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral fibre is toughness of character, so the word alone means resolve or backbone.

clue.text: Following reorganisation local chief left out adviser on success

indicators.note: reorganising the words local chief rearranges their letters
out says the letter for left is removed from the pool

explanation.surface: After a restructure, the local boss is ousted and a consultant brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following reorganisation' rearranges LOCALCHIEF and 'left out' removes one L.
explanation.definitionFit: A life coach advises clients on reaching their personal and career goals.

clue.text: Attractive female leaves deep impression

indicators.note: when the female letter leaves, it is taken away from the word

parts.note: fetching means attractive, as in a fetching hat

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman departs, leaving a profound mark on people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb of making a mark, but signals removal.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print made from lines incised into a metal plate, an impression cut deep.

clue.text: On radio give account of impressive film

indicators.note: radio is heard, not seen, so the word for giving an account is taken by its sound

parts.note: to tell is to recount or narrate
epic means grand and impressive

explanation.surface: A radio reviewer describes a magnificent film.
explanation.definitionFit: A telepic is a feature-length film made for television.

clue.text: Simon's ready in South America

parts.note: 'ready' is slang for cash, so this is the money named after a South American liberator called Simon

explanation.surface: Someone called Simon announces he is prepared, somewhere in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is British slang for money (from 'ready money'), not 'prepared'; Simón Bolívar's name is on Venezuela's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Venezuela's currency unit is named after the liberator Simón, so it is his money.

clue.text: Accept, say, free of charge almost every description of viewing aid

indicators.note: 'say' signals that the word for accepting is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: to buy an idea is to accept or believe it
FOC is the abbreviation for free of charge

indicators.note: almost the whole word loses its last letter

parts.note: every is all, as in 'all of them'

explanation.surface: Accept free of charge almost every description of a viewing aid, like a promise of free glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: BI sounds like 'buy'; 'almost' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Bifocal describes spectacle lenses with two focal regions, one for near and one for far sight.

clue.text: Through sun, hazy blue's impossible to fathom

parts.note: in can mean through, as in 'in that way'
Sol is the Latin name of the sun

indicators.note: something hazy is blurred and unclear, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: the word blue, with 's standing for 'is'

explanation.surface: Looking at the sun through a hazy blue sky, something seems impossible to work out.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of blue's reads as 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An insoluble problem cannot be solved or worked out.

clue.text: Crown emperor — and wave

parts.note: CR is a standard abbreviation for crown
IMP is short for Latin imperator, emperor, seen on coins

explanation.surface: A crowned emperor waves to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: IMP is the abbreviation of imperator found on old coins and inscriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimp hair is to give it small waves, and a crimp is such a wave.

clue.text: Frost at last heralded as a treasure

parts.note: hoar is a white frost on the ground

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word heralded is taken

explanation.surface: A frost, finally, is heralded as a treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard is a hidden store of valuables, such as buried coins.

clue.text: Single-minded European addicted to change

indicators.note: changing the letters puts them into a new order

explanation.surface: A determined European hooked on altering things.
explanation.definitionFit: Dedicated means wholly committed to one purpose, so focused and devoted.

clue.text: Tired arc light explodes engulfing leader of event

indicators.note: the shuffled letters swallow up the single letter
an explosion scatters the words arc light into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A worn-out arc lamp bursts and swallows up the start of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explodes' rearranges ARCLIGHT, which then engulfs the E from 'event'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means sluggish and lacking energy, like someone weary.

clue.text: Publication stage in Jewish image

indicators.note: the word for stage goes in the word for the image

parts.note: a teraph is an ancient Hebrew household idol
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A publication shows a stage in Jewish iconography.
explanation.walkthrough: TERAPH (plural teraphim) is a household idol from the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Telegraph is a British daily newspaper, the very paper printing this puzzle.

clue.text: Flier quarrels over Democrat's proposed law

indicators.note: turned over, the word for quarrels reads backwards

parts.note: rows are noisy arguments
D stands for Democrat in US politics
a bill is draft legislation before it is passed

explanation.surface: A politician fights over a Democrat's bill in Congress.
explanation.definitionFit: A swordbill is a South American hummingbird with a very long beak, so a bird that flies.

clue.text: Savouries from Greek island are special

parts.note: Samos is an island in the eastern Aegean
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Snacks from a Greek island are something special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' is not a verb but the metric unit of 100 square metres.
explanation.definitionFit: Samosas are fried pastries with a spicy filling, savoury snacks.

clue.text: Old Duke starts to build light aircraft. Weirdly eccentric!

indicators.note: weirdly means strangely, so these letters come out in odd order
the starts of the three words are their first letters

explanation.surface: An elderly duke begins building a light aircraft. How eccentric!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weirdly' comes at the end yet scrambles everything before it: OLD, D and BLA.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddball is a strange or eccentric person.

clue.text: Mel's a sweetheart

definitions.meaning: mel is Latin for the sweet substance bees make, a term still used in pharmacy
a term of endearment for a loved one

explanation.surface: Someone called Mel is a lovely person.
explanation.walkthrough: Mel is not a name here but the Latin word used in old pharmacy labels.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees' nectar product is mel in Latin, and it is also a pet name for a loved one.

clue.text: Northern Irish state, including heartlands of Omagh and Warrenpoint, is heaven

indicators.note: the state's letters include the two central letters

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: the heart of each word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Northern Ireland, from Omagh to Warrenpoint, described as paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: Omagh and Warrenpoint are towns in Northern Ireland; their middle letters are A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the Buddhist state of perfect bliss, loosely paradise.

clue.text: Poorly constructed deli in the old end of Bradford gave way under pressure

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the old word for 'the'

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of 'the', as in 'Ye Olde Shoppe'

indicators.note: a poorly built thing is out of shape, so these letters are rearranged
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A badly built delicatessen in the old part of Bradford collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bradford is a city in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielded means gave in or gave way when forced.

clue.text: Regularly sample red exotic wine

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every third one

explanation.surface: A wine lover samples an unusual red now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Every third letter of 'sample red exotic' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red Bordeaux from the region of that name in France.

clue.text: Sunspot for nudes?

parts.note: the Sun newspaper famously ran topless models on a particular page

explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid that long printed a topless model on the same page; 'sunspot' is that spot in the Sun, not a solar feature.
explanation.definitionFit: The page in the Sun newspaper known for its topless glamour photos.

clue.text: Irishman's pet

definitions.meaning: a nickname for a man from Ireland, from Patrick
a pet is a fit of temper or sulk

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' is not an animal but a bad mood, as in 'in a pet'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a familiar nickname for an Irish man and British slang for a fit of temper.

clue.text: Time to drink up and see Indian beauty spots

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: saki is a variant spelling of sake, Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Time to finish your drink and go sightseeing in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beauty spots' are marks on the forehead, not scenic places.
explanation.definitionFit: A tika is a coloured mark worn on the forehead by Hindus.

clue.text: Began to look round the centre of Seattle by day

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the day letter follows
the word for looking goes round the middle letter

parts.note: to stare is to look fixedly

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A visitor starts gazing around Seattle's downtown during the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Started is a past tense synonym for began, as in commenced.

clue.text: A weak king's battle with Germany becomes embarrassing

parts.note: W is an abbreviation for weak, in some reference works
K is the chess abbreviation for king
a war is a large-scale battle
D is Germany's international vehicle code, from Deutschland

explanation.surface: A feeble monarch going to war with Germany ends in humiliation.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward can mean causing embarrassment or discomfort, as in an uncomfortable silence.

clue.text: Spotted small portion of liver coated in fat

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: the letter is covered over by the word for fat

parts.note: podgy means chubby or plump

indicators.note: just a portion of the word liver, its first letter

explanation.surface: A small slice of liver is wrapped in fat, like a dish of faggots.
explanation.definitionFit: Splodgy describes something covered in blotches or patches, so blotched or spotted.

clue.text: Hot American group's manager

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
a band is a musical group; the 's links to the definition

explanation.surface: A hot American band's manager.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb, to husband is to manage resources thriftily; a husband was once a household manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband in older usage is a manager of a household or estate, as in a ship's husband.
